recommended_action.text: To clear Bus_29, raise the voltage set-point of Gen_bus7 from 1.000 to 1.012 p.u. Checked by a power flow: Bus_29 at 0.951 p.u., Gen_bus7 at 35.1 Mvar (range -15 to 60), no new violation.

No movement is certain to clear Bus_0 -> Bus_1 [L0]. The smallest single-source option is a 11.53 MW increase of Gen_bus1, which works only if Gen_bus1 has that headroom — not known here. Check its capability, or use several sources.

notes: Sensitivities are local finite differences; they support small corrective movements, not large counterfactuals.

relief_mw / relief_mvar is the movement that would bring the element to its limit assuming the source acts alone. A movement the source provably cannot make is withdrawn (null) rather than reported; max_deliverable_mw / max_deliverable_mvar then gives the most it could contribute.

A driver with `actionable: false` is uncontrollable — typically a load, included because it explains the regime. Its movement is reported as `would_require_mw` / `would_require_mvar`: a counterfactual that quantifies the driver, not an action anyone can take. Never present it as a recommendation; shedding demand is not corrective redispatch.
Each violation carries a `recommended_action` resolved here from the feasibility of every candidate movement. Report that rather than assembling an action from the driver fields.
The external grid is the slack and absorbs the resulting imbalance, so it is not perturbed.

For a voltage violation, `setpoint_levers` gives the voltage set-point of each of the most sensitive units that would clear it, checked by a full power flow (the violation cleared, the unit's bus within the band, its reactive output within its range, no new violation): `verified` says whether every check passed. A verified set-point change is the recommended action when one exists.

assistant:
Yes. On **5 January**, Bus_29 was undervoltage for one 15-minute interval, at **19:30**, reaching **0.944 p.u.** against the 0.950 p.u. lower limit. The warning threshold was reached at **19:15**, so there were **15 minutes’ warning**.

Holding Gen_bus7’s voltage set-point at **1.010 p.u. instead of 1.000 p.u.** from 19:15 through 19:30 was the smallest tested sufficient action. The checked power flows kept Bus_29 within its limit throughout, with no new violations.

This addresses the Bus_29 undervoltage; at 19:30, the assessment also found the line **Bus_0 → Bus_1 [L0]** overloaded at **107.6%**, which this result does not say was cleared. The study used the default **0.95 lagging load power factor**.

📋 Data source: measurements

assistant:
For the **earlier episode around 18:30**, Bus_29 was below 0.950 p.u. from **18:00 to 19:00** (five 15-minute samples), reaching **0.945 p.u.** at 18:30. The warning threshold was reached at **17:30**, giving **30 minutes’ warning**.

The prevention check found that raising Gen_bus7’s voltage set-point from **1.000 to 1.009 p.u.**, held from 17:30 through 19:00, would have kept Bus_29 within limits at every checked sample, with no new violations. This is separate from the later 19:30 undervoltage episode. At 18:30, Bus_0 → Bus_1 [L0] was also overloaded; the check addresses Bus_29 and does not establish that the existing overload was cleared.
